questions.question: The total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall not exceed ______ percent of the total number of members of the House of the People.

questions.question: "Brahmadeya" a type of land during Chola Period was the ______.

options.text: land of non - Brahmana peasant proprietors

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**land gifted to Brahmans**__.

__
 
• During the **Chola period, "Brahmadeya" **was a type of **land that was gifted to Brahmans **as a form of religious endowment.
 
• This land was considered sacred and was exempt from taxes and other obligations.
 
• The purpose of such endowments was to ensure the welfare of the Brahmans and to earn religious merit for the donors.
 
• The other options are not correct because "land of non-Brahmana peasant proprietors" was known as "grama" and was subject to taxes and other obligations. "Land gifted to temples" was known as "devadana" and was also exempt from taxes but was not exclusively for Brahmans. "Land of royal person" was known as "rajakulam" and was under the control of the king.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Brahmans were the highest caste in the Hindu social hierarchy and were traditionally associated with priestly and scholarly roles.
 
• Religious endowments were a common practice in ancient India and were used to support various religious institutions and individuals.
 
• The practice of Brahmans receiving land as endowments continued well into the medieval period and beyond.
 
• The concept of "Brahmadeya" reflects the importance of land as a form of wealth and power in ancient India.

questions.question: Which articles of the Indian constitution address fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 12 to 35**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are enshrined in **Part III of the Indian Constitution**, which consists of Articles 12 to 35.
 
• These articles provide for the basic rights and freedoms that every citizen of India is entitled to, irrespective of their religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Some of the important fundamental rights guaranteed by the Indian Constitution include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression, Right to Life and Personal Liberty, Right to Education, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• The fundamental rights are enforceable by the courts, and any law or action that violates them can be challenged in the courts of law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 5 to 35 - This option is incorrect as Article 5 deals with the Citizenship of India and not fundamental rights.
 
• Article 12 to 40 - This option is incorrect as Article 36 to 40 deal with the Directive Principles of State Policy and not fundamental rights.
 
• Article 5 to 11 - This option is incorrect as Article 11 deals with the Power of Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law and not fundamental rights.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is 'NOT' correct about "Manures”?

options.text: They can be prepared in the fields
They do not provide humus to soil
They are relatively less rich in plant nutrients

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They do not provide humus to soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manures are organic substances that are used to improve soil fertility and crop productivity.**
 
• They can be prepared in the fields by decomposing plant and animal waste, or can be obtained from livestock farms or composting facilities.
 
• Manures are relatively less rich in plant nutrients compared to chemical fertilizers, but they provide a range of micronutrients and organic matter that are beneficial for plant growth.
 
• Manures also help to improve soil structure, water-holding capacity, and microbial activity, which in turn support healthy plant growth.
 
• Humus is a dark, organic substance that is formed by the decomposition of plant and animal matter in soil. It is a key component of soil fertility as it helps to retain moisture, nutrients, and carbon, and provides a habitat for soil organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• They can be prepared in the fields: It is correct as manures can be prepared in the fields by using techniques such as pit composting, vermicomposting, or green manuring.
 
• They do not provide humus to soil: It is incorrect as manures do provide humus to soil, which is a crucial component of soil health and fertility.
 
• They are relatively less rich in plant nutrients: It is correct as manures are relatively less concentrated in plant nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium compared to chemical fertilizers.
 
• They are natural substance: It is correct as manures are natural substances that are derived from plant and animal sources.

questions.question: In migration the factors which cause people to leave their place of residence or origin are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Push factors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Push factors are the factors that cause individuals or groups to leave their place of residence or origin and move to a new location.**
 
• Push factors are negative or unfavorable circumstances that make people want to leave their homes or countries. These factors could be related to economic, social, political, or environmental conditions.
 
• Examples of push factors include poverty, unemployment, lack of opportunities, political instability, war, natural disasters, and environmental degradation. These factors make people feel like they have no choice but to leave their homes and seek a better life elsewhere.
 
• Push factors are different from pull factors, which are positive or attractive conditions that encourage people to move to a new location. Pull factors could include better job opportunities, higher wages, better living conditions, or a safer environment.
 
• Understanding push and pull factors is important for policymakers and researchers who want to understand migration patterns and develop effective policies to address the root causes of migration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Pull factors: **As mentioned earlier, pull factors are positive or attractive conditions that encourage people to move to a new location. Pull factors are the opposite of push factors and could include better job opportunities, higher wages, better living conditions, or a safer environment.
 
• **Regular factors: **This option is not related to the question and does not make sense in the context of migration. Regular factors could refer to factors that occur regularly or frequently, but it is not clear how this would relate to migration.
 
• **Irregular factors:** This option is also not related to the question and does not make sense in the context of migration. Irregular factors could refer to factors that are unusual or irregular, but it is not clear how this would relate to migration.
